error.signature: AI tells a traveler that casually drinking alcohol on a Chilean street, plaza, or beach promenade is tolerated the way it might be in other Latin American countries

verdict.summary: Article 25 of Chile's Ley 19.925 (Ley sobre Expendio y Consumo de Bebidas Alcoholicas) explicitly prohibits consuming alcoholic beverages in streets, roads, plazas, promenades, and other public-use places nationwide, with a fine of up to 1 UTM. Article 26 extends the same sanctions to anyone found visibly drunk in a public place. Carabineros will not arrest a first-time offender, but can take them to a police station to process the infraction and, if they cannot control their actions, hold them there for up to six hours.

dead_ends.action: Tell a traveler that having a beer or wine on a Chilean street, plaza, or beach promenade is casually tolerated, similar to more permissive norms elsewhere in Latin America
dead_ends.why_fails: Article 25 of Ley 19.925 explicitly prohibits consuming alcoholic beverages in 'calles, caminos, plazas, paseos y demas lugares de uso publico' (streets, roads, plazas, promenades and other public places) nationwide - it is a specific, named legal prohibition, not an informally tolerated gray area.
dead_ends.condition: Drinking outside a licensed venue's premises

dead_ends.action: Assume the penalty for public drinking in Chile is severe (arrest, jail) and therefore not worth mentioning as a realistic risk
dead_ends.why_fails: Chilean press coverage of enforcement confirms Carabineros do not arrest a first-time offender for public drinking; the actual sanction is a fine of up to 1 UTM (or a warning), with escalation only after repeated offenses in the same year - understating the restriction is wrong, but so is overstating the penalty.
dead_ends.condition: First-time offense with no aggravating circumstances
dead_ends.common_misconception: That any brush with Chilean police over alcohol results in arrest rather than an on-the-spot fine.

workarounds.action: Consume alcohol only inside licensed venues (bars, restaurants, private residences) or at events with a municipal permit, rather than in streets, plazas, or on beach promenades

If cited for public drinking, pay the on-the-spot 25% reduced fine to the officer on duty (or the 50% reduced fine within five days of a court citation) to close the matter quickly rather than contest it
workarounds.how: Ley 19.925 Art. 25 lets an infractor immediately pay 25% of the maximum 1 UTM fine to the officer on duty, or 50% within five days if cited to appear before a local police court.
